premise: Railway wagons once had to be joined by a person standing between them; every coupling idea failed until the knuckle locked itself.

hero_objects.name: knuckle coupler
hero_objects.look: A chunky cast-steel railway knuckle coupler, white with a yellow-and-black target decal on the side, the hinged knuckle painted orange.

hero_objects.name: freight wagon
hero_objects.look: A short white freight wagon with yellow-and-black target decals on each end, clean steel wheels, no markings.

beats.narration: Two wagons roll together, and you are standing between them.
beats.picture: Low angle between the buffers of two @Wagon ends closing in, the gap a body-width wide.

beats.narration: So why did anyone stand there?
beats.picture: Wide shot of a quiet rail yard, two @Wagon on one track a few metres apart.

beats.narration: A coupling must lock by itself the moment wagons touch.
beats.picture: Close side view of the empty coupling point at the end of a @Wagon.

beats.narration: First: a link and a pin, dropped in by hand.
beats.picture: A steel link hanging from a @Wagon end, a loose pin above its hole.

beats.narration: Someone guided the link as the wagons met.
beats.picture: Two @Wagon ends meeting with the link mid-air between them.

verdict.sub: a person stands in the gap

beats.narration: Second: a hook that drops over a bar.
beats.picture: A heavy steel hook on one @Wagon end above a bar on the other.

beats.narration: Fine on straight track. On a curve it bounces off.
beats.picture: Two @Wagon on a curved track, the hook jumping clear of the bar.

beats.narration: Third: a knuckle that swings shut.
beats.picture: Close three-quarter view of an open @Coupler on the end of a @Wagon.

beats.narration: Push the wagons together and it closes. Nobody between them.
beats.picture: Two @Coupler meeting head-on, knuckles swinging shut at the instant of contact.

beats.narration: Inside, the closing knuckle pushes a lock block aside.
beats.picture: Cutaway of the @Coupler with the lock block sliding aside as the knuckle turns.

beats.narration: Then gravity drops the lock behind it.
beats.picture: Cutaway of the @Coupler, the lock block fallen into place behind the closed knuckle.

beats.narration: A freight coupler holds roughly 350 tonnes of pull.
beats.picture: Side view of a long line of @Wagon stretching away, the first @Coupler in focus.

beats.narration: To uncouple, a lever lifts the lock from trackside.
beats.picture: Cross-section of the @Coupler lock with the lever raising the block.

beats.narration: So the next time two wagons roll together, nobody stands between them.
beats.picture: Low angle between the buffers of two @Wagon ends closing in, the gap empty.

loop_endings: So the next time two wagons roll together, nobody stands between them.
Two wagons roll together, and the gap stays empty.
That orange knuckle is why nobody stands there any more.

fact.claim: The 1893 Safety Appliance Act required automatic couplers on United States railroad cars.
fact.source_title: Library of Congress — U.S. Statutes at Large, vol. 27

titles.text: Why nobody stands between train wagons any more
The coupling that used to cost workers their hands
